svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Polysaccharides: polymers of glucose made by condensation."], [1, "Amylose: alpha-glucose, 1,4 bonds, unbranched; the chain coils into a helix."], [4.5, "Amylopectin: also 1,6 branches."], [7, "Glycogen: many more branches, so it is compact and releases glucose quickly."], [10, "Cellulose: beta-glucose, every other unit flipped; straight chains held together by hydrogen bonds into microfibrils."]]
svg.title: Starch, glycogen and cellulose
svg.desc: Amylose as an unbranched helix of alpha-glucose, amylopectin and glycogen with 1,6 branches, and cellulose as straight chains of beta-glucose linked by hydrogen bonds into microfibrils.
svg.text: Each hexagon is one glucose unit.

g.data-info: Unbranched chain of alpha-glucose joined by 1,4-glycosidic bonds; coils into a helix, so it is compact: a good energy store in plants.
g.text: helix: compact, insoluble → no effect on water potential

g.data-info: Alpha-glucose chains with 1,4 bonds and 1,6 branches about every 24–30 glucose units.
The energy store of animals and fungi: like amylopectin but much more branched (1,6 branches every 8–12 units), so it is very compact and has many ends where enzymes can release glucose quickly.

g.text: very branched: compact, many ends for enzymes to release glucose fast

g.data-info: Beta-glucose joined by 1,4 bonds, every other molecule inverted, giving straight chains. Hydrogen bonds between parallel chains form microfibrils of great tensile strength: plant cell walls.
g.text: β-glucose · 1,4 bonds · alternate units flipped · straight chains
hydrogen bonds (blue) link chains → microfibrils → cell wall strength
